How diagonal letter paths work in Word Tile Rush

Word Tile Rush accepts connected paths through neighboring cells, including diagonals. A path cannot reuse a tile, and only words in the game’s bundled list score.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 15, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read

Bottom line: Word Tile Rush uses a connected path, not a straight-line word search. Each next letter must be in a neighboring cell—horizontal, vertical, or diagonal—and a tile cannot be used twice in the same path.

Build and edit a path

Select at least three neighboring letters, then submit the spelling. The path preview shows the letters in order. Selecting an earlier tile in the path shortens it back to that point; selecting a non-neighboring tile or reusing a tile does not create a valid step.

Accepted words and board changes

The current game checks submitted words against a bundled local word set. A spelling that is familiar but absent from that set does not score. Each accepted word earns one point per letter; its tiles clear, the remaining column tiles settle, and a new row enters from below.

The round uses a 90-second clock that starts with the first selected letter and pauses when the page is hidden or loses focus. Play ends when time expires or the rising grid reaches the top. Review the current Word Tile Rush page for the controls and live status.
